title: MV Help with two directional facing character

posts.author: HipSlip
posts.body:
Hi internet people.
So I'm very new to RPG Maker and very new to forum (just made this account today so I apologize for any guideline violations).
Anyway I bought MV as an xmas gift to myself and so far I really like it.
But I've been scratching my head for the last two days trying to solve this problem.
My sprite is intentionally designed to only face two directions, left or right. And for the up and down sections of the sprite sheet I just copy pasted the left and right sections to it. Naturally causing the character to always be facing left when going up and facing right going down. I want my character to stay facing the direction they were in when I move them up and down. The best example that comes to mind is like how the characters move in Castle Crashers.
This isn't my entire plugin loadout but the relevant ones I'm using are QPlus, QMovement, and GALV Character Animation.
I tried adding the <retainDir> comment to the event on my test map thinking that would solve it but my problem persists.
I also tried checking the direction fix box and adding some code but I didn't really know what I was doing.
I'll post screenshots and list my plugins and everything if I need to, I'm new and not familiar with how things are formatted here.
Any help would be greatly appreciated.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Don't know about the plugins, but isn't one engine way of doing it having direction fix ON + a parallel event that checks (you can use scripts so all happen on same frame I guess):
if left is pressed -> direction fix OFF, turn left, direction fix ON
if right is pressed -> direction fix OFF, turn right, direction fix ON
EDIT: You also need to put conditionals that only set the move route if the player isn't already facing that direction (so that it doesn't block movement by activating constantly). Also, I tested it out for fun and you need to use the script forms for fluidity, like:
$gamePlayer.setDirectionFix(false); $gamePlayer.setDirection(6); $gamePlayer.setDirectionFix(true);
Of course you could also make a plugin to edit the code.
